big_case.notes: Significant constitutional dispute over whether Turner v. Safley or heightened scrutiny governs sex-segregated housing and cross-sex searches of transgender inmates in correctional facilities, drawing a 23-state amicus brief and a CVSG, though resolved via a GVR in light of West Virginia v. B.P.J. and United States v. Skrmetti rather than plenary merits review because of a party-presentation vehicle defect below.

leakage.notes: Forward-mode run executed on 2026-09-18, prior to the Solicitor General's invited brief (2026-09-25) and the Court's GVR disposition (2026-11-09). Retrieval log and retrieval.md match completely and show only pre-disposition docket checks and precedent lookups on West Virginia v. B.P.J.

central_claims.basis: On September 25, 2026, the Solicitor General filed an amicus brief arguing that the Tenth Circuit erred on both questions presented and recommending that the Court grant, vacate, and remand in light of West Virginia v. B.P.J. and United States v. Skrmetti.
central_claims.claim: The Solicitor General's invited brief will align with petitioners on the merits (given federal BOP biological-sex policies) and likely recommend a grant or GVR.

central_claims.basis: The Solicitor General's brief (pp. 17, 21-22) relied directly on the Tenth Circuit's party-presentation holding to conclude that the petition is an unsuitable vehicle for plenary review of Question 1.
central_claims.claim: Question 1 faces a serious party-presentation vehicle obstacle because petitioners conceded intermediate scrutiny below and the Tenth Circuit declined to decide whether Turner v. Safley applies.

central_claims.basis: The Solicitor General's brief (pp. 17, 22) agreed that there is no circuit split on Question 2 and that plenary review is unwarranted because B.P.J. and Skrmetti independently foreclose respondent's claims.
central_claims.claim: Question 2 is an unattractive vehicle for plenary review because it arises at the Rule 12(b)(6) stage, lacks a circuit split, and leaves the abusive-manner search claim alive below.

central_claims.basis: Although the forecast document identified an SG-recommended GVR as the residual summary pathway, it predicted plenary review limited to Question 1 as the primary grant route; instead, the Court adopted the SG's recommendation and GVR'd in light of B.P.J. and Skrmetti on November 9, 2026.
central_claims.claim: Conditional on a grant, the Court is much more likely to grant plenary review limited to Question 1 than to issue a GVR (12% conditional summary-disposition route).

central_claims.basis: The petition was distributed a third time on October 14, 2026 for the November 6, 2026 conference and resolved on November 9, 2026 with no further CVSG.
central_claims.claim: After the Solicitor General's brief is filed, the petition will be distributed at least once more without a second CVSG.
